:::{#exm-cosine-sine-unit-circle}
#### The unit circle and the angle $\pi/3$

Take $\angpar = \pi/3$, one sixth of the way round the circle.
@fig-cosine-sine-unit-circle shows the point reached,
$(\cos\angpar, \sin\angpar)$, and its two coordinates.
The point is a vertex of a regular hexagon inscribed in the unit circle,
whose sides have the same length as its radius,
so the point is at distance $1$ from $(1, 0)$.
Writing $(x_1, x_2) = (\cos\angpar, \sin\angpar)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
1 &= (x_1 - 1)^2 + x_2^2 \\
&= x_1^2 + x_2^2 - 2 x_1 + 1 \\
&= 2 - 2 x_1,
\end{aligned}
$$

so $\cos(\pi/3) = x_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}$,
and then $\sin(\pi/3) = \sqrt{1 - \tfrac{1}{4}} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
To three decimal places these are
`r round(cos(pi / 3), 3)` and `r round(sin(pi / 3), 3)`.
As @thm-cosine-sine-identity says, the squared coordinates add to
`r round(cos(pi / 3)^2 + sin(pi / 3)^2, 3)`.

:::{#fig-cosine-sine-unit-circle}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: !expr knitr::is_html_output()
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The unit circle in the plane. A radius from the origin to the point
#|   (0.5, 0.866) on the circle makes an angle of pi/3 with the positive
#|   horizontal axis. A dashed vertical segment of length 0.866, the sine,
#|   joins the point to the horizontal axis, and the horizontal axis from
#|   the origin to 0.5 is marked as the cosine.

# angle in radians, and the point it reaches on the unit circle
angle <- pi / 3
point <- data.frame(x1 = cos(angle), x2 = sin(angle))

# points around the whole circle
circle <- data.frame(t = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200))
circle$x1 <- cos(circle$t)
circle$x2 <- sin(circle$t)

# arc from angle 0 to the chosen angle
arc <- data.frame(t = seq(0, angle, length.out = 50))
arc$x1 <- 0.25 * cos(arc$t)
arc$x2 <- 0.25 * sin(arc$t)

unit_circle_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_path(data = circle, ggplot2::aes(x1, x2)) +
  ggplot2::geom_path(data = arc, ggplot2::aes(x1, x2)) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = point$x1, yend = point$x2),
    colour = "firebrick"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = point$x1, y = 0, xend = point$x1, yend = point$x2),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = point$x1, yend = 0),
    colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = point, ggplot2::aes(x1, x2)) +
  ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0.4, y = 0.1, label = "angle") +
  ggplot2::annotate(
    "text", x = point$x1 / 2, y = -0.09, label = "cosine"
  ) +
  ggplot2::annotate(
    "text", x = point$x1 + 0.05, y = point$x2 / 2, label = "sine",
    hjust = 0
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_equal() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x1", y = "x2") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  plotly::ggplotly(unit_circle_plot)
} else {
  unit_circle_plot
}
```

The unit circle with the point at angle $\pi/3$.
Its horizontal coordinate is the cosine and its vertical coordinate is the sine.
